headline: Intel, SK hynix, Samsung and Micron report memory supply constraints amid AI demand growth
summary: Micron’s FY2026 Form 10-K, filed 3 September, states that AI-driven memory and storage demand growth outpaced industry supply and led to supply-allocation decisions and higher pricing. In separate Q3 disclosures on 28–29 October, SK hynix said memory supply was not keeping pace and forecast demand exceeding supply through 2030; Samsung reported memory capacity constraints and forecast 2027 AI-driven demand far exceeding industry supply; Intel said industry-wide memory, substrate and other component constraints affected results, while demand for some data-center products exceeded available supply. These are company-reported conditions from non-identical reporting periods, not independent market measurements. Intel’s DCAI segment spans CPUs, AI accelerators and other data-center products, so its figures do not isolate AI demand or memory exposure.
